record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Sublinear vertex-reinforced random walk on Z
record.original_question: Consider a vertex-reinforced random walk on the integers that jumps to nearest neighbors, starts with weight one at each vertex, and from location x at time n jumps to x+1 with probability proportional to w(1+ell_n(x+1)), where ell_n(y) is the local time at y by time n. If the weight function is sublinear in the sense that w(x)=o(x^alpha) for some alpha < 1, is the walk recurrent?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15 Suppose that w(x) = o(x α ) for some α < 1. Is this process recurrent?
Consider a vertex reinforced random walk on the integers

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a nearest-neighbor random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ defined as follows. Fix a weight function $w:\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\to(0,\infty)$ with $w(0)=1$. For each vertex $y\in\mathbb{Z}$ and time $n\ge 0$, let
$$\ell_n(y)=\#\{0\le k\le n : X_k=y\}$$
be the local time at $y$ up to time $n$. Set $X_0=0$, and given the history up to time $n$ with $X_n=x$, set
$$P(X_{n+1}=x+1\mid \mathcal{F}_n)=\frac{w(\ell_n(x+1))}{w(\ell_n(x+1))+w(\ell_n(x-1))},\qquad P(X_{n+1}=x-1\mid \mathcal{F}_n)=\frac{w(\ell_n(x-1))}{w(\ell_n(x+1))+w(\ell_n(x-1))}.$$
Suppose the weight function is sublinear in the sense that $w(x)=o(x^\alpha)$ as $x\to\infty$ for some $\alpha<1$. Determine whether the process $(X_n)$ is necessarily recurrent, i.e., whether $X_n=0$ for infinitely many $n$ almost surely.
artifact.status_search_result: The full question for all sublinear weights $w(x)=o(x^\alpha)$ with $\alpha<1$ appears to remain open. Partial results are known: vertex-reinforced random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$ with weights of order $k^\alpha$ for $\alpha\in[0,1/2)$ has been shown to be recurrent (Schapira and related work), and a 0-1 law holds in this regime. The range $\alpha\in[1/2,1)$ has not been fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Vertex-reinforced random walk on Z with sub-square-root weights is recurrent
status_evidence.snippet: Vertex-reinforced random walk on Z with weights of order k^alpha, for alpha in [0,1/2), is recurrent.
status_evidence.claim: Recurrence is established for sub-square-root weights, i.e., the case alpha<1/2.

status_evidence.title: A 0-1 law for vertex-reinforced random walks on Z with weight of order k^alpha, alpha in [0,1/2)
status_evidence.snippet: VRRW on Z with weight of order k^alpha, alpha in [0,1/2), is either almost surely recurrent or almost surely transient.
status_evidence.claim: A 0-1 law is known in the sub-square-root regime, but the full sublinear regime remains open.
